questions.stem: A manufacturer wants to silver-plate a steel spoon. How should the electrolysis cell be set up?

options.text: Steel spoon as the anode; silver as the cathode; silver nitrate solution as electrolyte
Steel spoon as the cathode; silver as the anode; silver nitrate solution as electrolyte
Steel spoon as the cathode; carbon as the anode; sodium chloride solution as electrolyte
Silver as the cathode; steel spoon as the anode; sulfuric acid as electrolyte

questions.explanation: In electroplating, the object to be plated must be the cathode (negative electrode) so that metal ions from solution are deposited onto it. The plating metal (silver) is used as the anode, which dissolves to replace the ions removed from solution. The electrolyte must contain ions of the plating metal (silver nitrate).

questions.stem: During the electroplating of a brass key with nickel, what happens at the anode?

options.text: Nickel ions are deposited as nickel metal
The nickel anode dissolves, releasing Ni2+ ions into the solution
Hydrogen gas is produced
The brass key dissolves

questions.explanation: At the anode, the nickel metal is oxidised: Ni -> Ni2+ + 2e-. The nickel anode gradually dissolves, releasing nickel ions into the electrolyte solution. This replaces the Ni2+ ions that are being deposited at the cathode (the brass key), maintaining the concentration of the electrolyte.

questions.stem: A car bumper is chrome-plated to improve its appearance and prevent rusting. Which property of chromium makes it suitable for this purpose?

options.text: Chromium is very reactive and attracts oxygen away from the steel
Chromium is shiny and resistant to corrosion, forming a protective barrier
Chromium is cheaper than the steel underneath
Chromium is a good electrical conductor

questions.explanation: Chromium is chosen for electroplating because it has an attractive shiny appearance and is highly resistant to corrosion. It forms a thin protective layer that prevents water and oxygen from reaching the steel underneath, thus preventing rusting. It acts as a physical barrier rather than through sacrificial protection.

questions.stem: A jeweller electroplates copper rings with gold. If the electrolyte concentration decreases over time, what does this suggest about the anode?

options.text: The anode is made of an inert material like carbon, not gold
The anode is dissolving too quickly
The current is too high
The cathode is dissolving instead of the anode

questions.explanation: If the electrolyte concentration is decreasing, metal ions are being removed at the cathode but not being replaced at the anode. This means the anode is inert (e.g., carbon or platinum) rather than being made of the plating metal. A gold anode would dissolve and replace the Au ions being deposited, maintaining the concentration.

questions.stem: Why might a food can be electroplated with tin rather than left as bare steel?

options.text: Tin makes the can stronger so it can withstand higher pressures
Tin is non-toxic and corrosion-resistant, preventing contamination of food and rusting of the steel
Tin is magnetic, which helps in recycling
Tin is a better conductor of heat, helping food cook faster

questions.explanation: Tin is used to coat food cans because it is non-toxic (safe for contact with food), resistant to corrosion, and unreactive with most foods. The thin tin layer acts as a barrier that prevents the steel from rusting and stops iron ions from contaminating the food. Steel alone would rust and taint the food.
